decision: The prototype uses Python with Lark, starting on Earley and moving the same grammar toward LALR once the syntax settles.
reason: Agent fluency in Python is the main metric, Earley accepts arbitrary context-free grammars and can show ambiguities explicitly, and the grammar file doubles as the readable syntax spec.

decision: The syntax author's hand-off grammar is adopted byte for byte as the single grammar.
reason: The walker needs one grammar, the grammar is tested against the whole snippet corpus, a byte copy can be compared with cmp, and a grammar of our own would be a second source.

decision: A status report says the walker parser is LALR with the tab indenter and provably free of ambiguity.
Lexing and parsing become separable programs (lex | parse) by setting the Lark lexer to basic.
reason: PSJ wants the two programs separable, and the agent measured that nothing in the grammar depends on parser state, with identical trees on 29 examples, 3411 strings and 20000 random inputs.

decision: The tree-sitter grammar is generated from the Lark grammar plus lex.py while the indentation scanner stays hand-written.
reason: No converter exists, tree-sitter rules may not match empty while an empty frame is legal FPL, and generating the grammar lets the hand-written remainder be measured.

decision: A module runs first and turns source into code the LALR grammar can read.
reason: An LALR grammar cannot count nesting or indentation.

decision: LALR is fed by a tab indenter and the Earley parse is dropped as the main path.
reason: The grammar declares indent and dedent tokens that only an indenter can make, so the skeleton Earley parse could not run the grammar.

decision: A line of form feeds joins the blank run of newline tokens.
reason: A form feed cut the newline run in two, so render then parse was not idempotent.

decision: Body tab indentation is not produced inside unclosed string pairs.
The grammar reference records the layout decisions tabs, no Postel, no semicolon and no colon, with strict indentation and the space-after-indentation rule living in lex.py only.
The tree-sitter scanner keeps a level stack like the Lark indenter and refuses a dedent to a level that was never opened.
reason: A verifier finding was reproduced by running code.

decision: Indentation is held strict with tabs only, and no bracket stays open across a dedent below the line that opened it.
Strings and comments never reach Lark, because the pre-lexer counts them by their own pair and stashes the interior, and indentation is held strict there.
The pair pass is split from the strict indentation rule so the FON reader can reuse the pair pass.
reason: FON documents may be indented with spaces which the strict rule would refuse, and copying the pair pass into a second file is forbidden by house style.

decision: Strings and block comments are counted by a pre-lexer and indentation by the Lark indenter, with LALR over the grammar file.
A small pre-lexer runs before Lark and the grammar file is deliberately left free of counting.
reason: A context-free grammar cannot say which closing quote pairs with which opener when the same pair nests, or how far a line may dedent while a bracket is open.

decision: A pair is counted by its own closer only, so an opener inside a string or comment is plain text and two pairs never overlap.
A string opener glued to a word is padded, and the placeholder and pad keep the opener offset.
reason: The placeholder must be its own token, and mutation testing checked the offsets.

decision: Strings, raw strings and block comments are Dyck pairs counted by the pre-lexer.
reason: Counting as pairs lets nesting work without escapes.

decision: A string becomes one placeholder character in the code while its interior stays in the source for the pair reader.
A block comment that opens an indented line leaves the tabs in place, recorded as a hole, while block comments otherwise leave no indentation and separate words.
reason: It was the one branch no test reached.

decision: Comments get a place in the tree, attachment is tree position, and the trivia module goes away.
reason: It removes the problem that pushed comments into the newline run.

decision: A comment line that heads a block is refused as unimplemented until design decides whether the block runs as quotations or as lines.
reason: There is no evaluator yet.

decision: A block comment alone on a line opens no block.
reason: The bootstrap parser drops the comment and produces no block, so tree-sitter must agree.

decision: A block comment becomes nothing.
The printer reproduces the opening-line tabs after a multi-line string, and an empty frame beside a bar prints as its bar.
reason: Joining frames with a bar would open a line with a space which the pre-lexer refuses, and print then parse must be the identity.

decision: One ASCII pair with a prefix letter naming the reader was proposed, then heredoc-style named delimiters, with no decision recorded.
reason: English text is full of apostrophes and ASCII has only four bracket pairs, three of them taken.

decision: Every code character keeps its source offset.
reason: Errors and spans must land in the source.

decision: The verbatim flag on one-character pads is dropped and tests now check spans and refusal offsets.
reason: The flag said nothing because mutants survived, and every refusal row sat at offset 0.

decision: The REPL takes body depth from the pre-lexer origin per character instead of from the physical line.
reason: The pre-lexer drops comments and keeps tabs, so depth must be what the parser sees.

decision: Lines are split by newline only, and editor-server columns are sent as UTF-16 code units.
reason: A verifier finding was reproduced.

decision: Positions stay in the source, so every code character keeps its origin.
Every AST node gets a source span from day one.
reason: A hobby language lives or dies on the quality of its parse and type errors, and Earley error messages in Lark are weak.

decision: Nesting deeper than the recursion limit gets one refusal at 1:1, recorded as a hole.
reason: A recursion error appears at about 100 brackets or 400 block levels, and every refusal must be an FplError.

decision: A stray closer is refused and the comment scan reads the pre-lexed code instead of string interiors, both recorded as holes.
reason: Each reuses a mechanism already in force.

decision: The FON reader checks depth with a linear scan before Lark.
reason: No visitor error can wrap a refusal, the recursive depth function could exhaust the stack, and the scan names the unclosed opener.

decision: The REPL head verdict comes from a parse of the whole input.
reason: A reviewer agent found a bug when a head stood after a block-comment closer on the same line.

decision: Editor diagnostics are the interpreter own FplError, at most one per source.
reason: It is the cheapest route.

decision: Refusals are placed at a line and column in the source, and an unclosed pair is reported where the source runs out.
New tests call the pre-lexer directly.
reason: The pre-lexer refusals were tested only through the parser.

decision: Mutants that never terminate are killed by a direct test of the counted function.
reason: Otherwise the kill depended on timing.

decision: PRs stay draft until the owner gives the CrossHair lane a time budget, since it never finishes on the parser properties.
Both LALR parsers are built once at import, taking 17 ms, instead of through a cache.
reason: CrossHair bypasses functools caches and the build never finishes under its tracer, and a 300 s timeout went down to 31 s.

decision: On the project own sources LALR is about 33 times faster than Earley with the indenter, with identical trees on 31 of 31 files.
reason: Earley is 25 to 43 times slower and uses about 8 times the memory at 100k tokens, so a page should state the constant factor and memory and not a different complexity class.

decision: A CI gate asserts zero ambiguity.
reason: Earley in Lark accepts ambiguous grammars quietly and it bites months later.

decision: Lexing splits on whitespace with self-delimiting delimiters, enclosures are Dyck pairs in the grammar, indentation is the invisible pair, token shape is a regular post-pass, and named closers stay outside as Type-1.
The ambiguity check is split in two, with Earley over the full grammar and indenter for the corpus and drawn programs coming from a block-free grammar.
reason: An indenter cannot run inside a derivation.

decision: The hand-off grammar let a frame match nothing, which Earley showed as ambiguity in 26 of 29 examples, and the fix brought the counts to zero with no LALR conflicts, later replaced by G6.
Grammar fixes go in as spec commits for PSJ or Caesura to accept or rewrite.
reason: The grammar is the oracle.

decision: There is one frame rule and a frame may be empty, an empty bracket pair is distinct from one with a bar, and comments are NOTE and DOC tokens kept in the tree.
reason: Comments have value, so they are tokens kept in the tree and neither ignored nor folded into the newline token.

decision: Every comment body is an FML tree that hangs on an AST node by identity.
reason: PSJ wants all comments to support FML, and FML is a Dyck language and therefore always well-formed.

decision: Overlap through named closers is switched on only by a profile, and without it the pre-lexer refuses overlap while code stays tree-shaped.
reason: The profile is part of the interface hash and counted Dyck pairs can only form trees.

decision: The grammar is deliberately structural: every word is one token, shape is the affix pass, and strings, comments and indentation are counted outside it.
reason: Editor tooling can then come from the grammar file plus lex.py.

decision: TypeScript with Ohm and OCaml with Menhir were rejected.
reason: In Ohm a missing semantic action fails at runtime, and OCaml brings opam and dune friction and a thinner corpus.

decision: The frontend is layered, with a dumb parse module, desugaring to a core AST, and errors shown with line, column and caret.
reason: It keeps the change-syntax loop cheap.

decision: A test pins the indenter terminal names to the grammar.
reason: A renamed terminal would leave the indenter silently counting nothing.

decision: The counted function returns None for an unclosed opener instead of -1.
reason: A slip in -1 still gives a valid offset and caused a non-terminating scan.

decision: Code is ASCII outside strings and string contents are raw UTF-8, with PSJ adoption not recorded.
reason: BPE token cost, and a lexer on pure ASCII can use byte tables and SIMD and jump over string contents by scanning for quotes.

decision: The colon is not a lexer token, and the agent recommends making it explicit in three steps.
reason: It leads to measured silent misparses.

decision: Comment bodies stay opaque, the four string and comment pairs stay reserved, and printing a parse reproduces the source byte for byte.
reason: FML can then parse clean text later.

decision: The indenter waiver is file-level.
The bar is a self-delimiting token, measured to make the bar-equals operator fail, and the route is left to PSJ.
reason: PSJ wants claims checked inside the language.

decision: The seed FON is braced and read by LALR while FON is intended to be postfix ASCII, as an ADR draft.
Highlighting is generated from the grammar terminals plus lex.py, leaving 0 unscoped characters on 31 programs.
lex.py is tangled from a literate page byte for byte.
reason: The gates stay unchanged.

decision: A literate lex page states that a grammar is a poor counter and names nested strings and comments, strict indentation, and token shape by affixes as the things needing counting.
reason: A Lark grammar cannot count these.
